prior_art.basis: Independent review by claude-independent-prior-art-reviewer-20261106: No open or discoverable solution provides a decent home for every family, so the Main KPI of 2,000,000,000 people newly housed is unmet. UN-Habitat estimates about 100 million people are homeless, about one in four live in housing that harms their health, safety and prosperity, and about 3 billion people (40% of the world) will need adequate housing by 2030, which requires 96,000 new affordable units every day (https://unhabitat.org/topic/housing). The largest programmes are national subsidy schemes such as India's PMAY-Gramin, whose evaluations are regional and descriptive (https://doi.org/10.56975/ijcrt.v13i6.288811), and the lower-cost construction routes remain unproven at scale: a 2026 review of 3D-printed affordable housing finds unresolved scalability, cost and regulatory barriers (https://doi.org/10.3390/buildings16020343). Honest limit: building methods, subsidy and cooperative housing models are known and published, so this is chiefly a finance, land and governance problem, and tasks that restate known programmes are not new work; tasks must target a new, checkable piece, such as a verified cost-per-unit reduction method, a land-tenure or targeting method, or a validated housing-adequacy measurement from imagery.
